+From 28 November 2026, a new Onshore Application Charge applies to certain Student visa applications. This charge is in addition to the existing Visa Application Charge. Exemptions apply to some applicants. Learn more at Fees and charges for visas.
 Alert: Student visa 500 & 590 changes
 Changes to Student visa application rulesFrom 2 October 2026, there are new rules for Student visas (subclass 500) and Student Guardian visas (subclass 590). The rules change who can apply for and be granted a visa while in Australia, and whether family members can be included in a Student visa application. For an overview of the changes, visit the Student visa changes information page. Make sure you know how the new rules affect you before making visa, study, travel or relocation plans.
 Visit Australia to participate in a course of study.

 Further student visa From 2 October 2026, new rules apply to current Student visa holders who want to lodge another Student visa application while in Australia. Most Student visa holders can no longer apply for a further Student visa in Australia. If you hold a student visa you can only apply in Australia if you meet an exemption. If you do not meet an exemption category, you must apply from outside Australia. If you hold a Student visa but are no longer eligible to apply for another Student visa while in Australia, you will need to lodge your next application from outside Australia. To help minimise your time outside Australia and any interruptions to your studies, make sure you prepare your application and supporting documents before leaving Australia. For more information about applying from outside Australia, see the Student visa changes. Applications lodged before 2 October 2026 will continue to be assessed under the rules that were in place when they were lodged. This includes applications that included family members. Other visas If your Student visa will expire before your graduation, you might be eligible for a Visitor visa (subclass 600) to attend your graduation. You will need a letter from your education provider with the date of your graduation. If you hold or held a Student visa and completed specific qualifications in Australia in the last six months, you might be eligible for a Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485). If you want to stay longer for other reasons, you must apply for a new visa that suits your circumstances. Explore your visa options.
 Include family in some circumstances
 From 2 October 2026, new rules apply to including family members in Student visa applications. Most Student visa applicants can no longer include family members. This also applies to people applying for a further Student visa. If you submitted your application before 2 October 2026, we will assess it under the rules that were in place on the date you applied. This also applies to applications that included family members. You cannot include family members (partners and children) in your Student visa application lodged unless you meet an exemption category. Your family members cannot apply as a subsequent entrant (at a later time, separate from your application) in any circumstance. For Student visas, your family member is: your partner, or your or your partner's dependent child who is unmarried and has not turned 18 years of age. We cannot grant a Student visa to your child if they have turned 18 years at the time your visa is finalised. They need to apply for their own visa. Newborn child If you have a child while holding a Student visa or while your Student visa application is being processed, different arrangements apply depending on where the child is born. Child born in Australia: The child automatically holds the same visa as their parent Child born in Australia: The primary applicant can include the child in a further student visa application lodged in Australia if they are eligible to apply and include family in Australia under an exemption category. Child born outside Australia while a Student visa application is being processed: The primary applicant can include the child in the application before a decision is made, provided they meet an exemption category to include family members. Find out what to do if you have a child. Family members who apply for the visa must meet our requirements for health and character. For more information about if you are eligible to include family members in your application, see Meet an exemption if you want to include family members on the Eligibility page. Check the annual school costs you will need to pay for any dependent children to go to either public or private schools in Australia. For more information see ‘Evidence you have enough money for your stay’ section under Gather documents.
